blocks.text: In “Father Country, I Do Love You”, on view at the Guggenheim in New York, Taryn Simon follows the life of an unnamed federal agent through 42 cases he worked on during his career. Together they become a thread for reflecting on American society and on the United States’ tentacular presence in other countries’ internal affairs.
By Gaia Squarci. Photographs by Taryn Simon.

blocks.caption: Taryn Simon, There’s no start or finish, 2026 (detail). © 2026 Taryn Simon

blocks.text: Simon dedicates this body of work to her father, who worked abroad for the US government before switching to manufacturing pool tables and arcade games. She never heard his full story, and since his Alzheimer’s diagnosis she knows she never will. Because the agent is never named, he becomes one of countless people who carry out American policy, as Simon puts it, “without access to the entire picture.”

blocks.caption: Taryn Simon, You have to backfill it, 2026 (detail). © 2026 Taryn Simon

blocks.text: The exhibition raises questions about even the most solid values the country stands on. Democracy is one of them: a chapter traces it back to its origins in ancient Greece, in a reflection that echoes contemporary cases. “There was no prison, but if you were convicted you were kicked off a hill, which is very steep. If you survived, it meant you deserved a second chance.”

blocks.caption: Taryn Simon, You have to backfill it, 2026 (video still). © 2026 Taryn Simon
Taryn Simon, We were the diggers, 2026 (detail). © 2026 Taryn Simon

blocks.text: Photography is one of several media used to build a complex system of meaning. Text provides the context and, through the agent’s own words, sometimes exposes the failures of a system he never truly questions at its core. The photographs rely on their power to evoke, and they deliberately give up on explanations. Simon’s visual language is devoid of pathos even when she addresses a terrorist attack, a murder case or child pornography, and the power of the work comes from this restraint.

blocks.caption: Taryn Simon, Earth two, 2026. Color video, with sound, 23 min., 38 sec. © 2026 Taryn Simon

blocks.text: A game that visitors can play, recalling those Simon’s father once built, runs through the whole exhibition. In her words, ‘A single act of participation and touch unfolds in ways that can’t be calculated.’

blocks.caption: Taryn Simon, A squad agent informed me I’d be babysitting, 2026 (detail). © 2026 Taryn Simon
Taryn Simon, Like kryptonite, 2026 (detail). © 2026 Taryn Simon

blocks.text: The exhibition “Father Country, I Do Love You” is on view at the Guggenheim Museum in New York City until March 14, 2027.
